[spoiler=[b]UREV Welfare Initiative - Project 2030[/b] 
[u]18th Novemember, 2026[/u]]

President Valeri Puteyr made many promises under a connected plan that was coined 'Project 2030', the aim of which was to increase standards of living and equality by 2030, just before the end of his presidency. During election, Project 2030 was lambasted by both Nationals and Prosperity for being extensive tasks that would require large funds to be effectively completed, and critics had doubts that a single term would be enough. Prosperity especially feared that relying too much on the tax from the White Sea could see the state become fiscally unstable and could see a return to Volkovian budget arrangements.

With Valeri securing a second-term his cabinet remained unchanged, and following the ceremonies held at the Government Plaza, would begin negotiations with Nationals and Prosperity to attempt a successful push of the Welfare Initiative through the United Assembly. Analysts expected major changes to what was initially promised by Valeri during his campaign, Prosperity was never going to accept such spending, though major pressure was being put on the Nationals from their voter-base and some voices in Nationals were open to a much more limited vision for Project 2030.

18th November 2026 saw the Federalists propose the first package of the UREV Welfare Initiative, step one of three to focus on the lower 10% income group. The first step would be implemented in December of 2026, and include a nationwide monetary package to those who fit a certain criteria, most important of which being within the lower 10% of incomes. This monetary package will range in monetary amount to each individual decided by a few factors, though is expected to at maximum only go up to $2000 United Dollars. This would coincide with a $1.5 billion stimulus aimed towards small businesses, allowing them the necessary funds to increase production and cater to the increase demand in the lower income brackets.

Valeri has called it a large step towards creating jobs in lower income areas, while his critics warn that the initiative may not play out as he expects. Prosperity calls for fiscal responsibility and argues that lower regulations to businesses will create an influx of new jobs, while Nationals warns that the central government taking a major part in this initiative will make it ineffective and advises that local entities handle the welfare initiative.

Though with the large amount of criticism the government has faced for this decision, it is expected for step one to be accepted by the United Assembly with the Federalists, Greens, and large parts of Nationals vowing to have it pass. Some in the Federalist bloc have been puzzled by Valeri's insistence on passing Project 2030 initiatives as soon as possible, believing that Federatlists could gain an easy majority in the upcoming 2027 Assembly Elections.

[i]"While I do understand why many suggest I wait for the Assembly Elections, there is no guarantee Federalists will secure enough of a majority to easily pass Project 2030 initiatives. A mixed approach, that takes into account the opinions of the other parties and the people they represent, is fair for all of UREV. I believe a mixed approach is more cautious and minimises potential economic risks that may arise." [/i]- President Valeri summarised his decisions in a social media post.[/spoiler]
